title: The AC Generator
summary: Turn a coil in a field: find the peak and instantaneous emf, timing, and how changes scale the output.
subject: physics
learningOutcome: The student can find the peak and instantaneous emf of a rotating coil, the timing of the peak from the speed, and how the peak emf changes with turns, speed and field.

levels.title: Peak and instant
levels.adds: Baseline: ε = NB Aω sin ωt, with the peak NBAω (Example 6.10).
hints: The peak emf is N B A ω, with A in m² and ω = 2πf.
The emf is zero when the plane of the coil is at right angles to the field.
At an angle θ from there, the emf is the peak times sin θ.

levels.title: Revolutions per minute
levels.adds: New idea: convert rev/min to rad/s, and the emf takes a quarter of a turn to go from zero to its peak.
hints: Zero to peak is a quarter of that.

levels.title: Change the generator
levels.adds: Apply it: the peak emf is proportional to N, B, A and ω, so the changes multiply.
hints: The peak is proportional to each of the number of turns, the field and the speed.
Multiply the factors together, do not add them.
Start from the known peak emf.

misconceptions: The emf is greatest when the plane of the coil is at right angles to the field
Doubling both the speed and the field doubles the peak emf
The emf of a generator is constant
